sentiment.rationale: Guidance for 2026 is for organic revenue growth of 4%-5% and comparable currency-neutral EPS growth of 5%-6%, which is in line with the long-term growth algorithm and not raised above prior expectations. The 2025 results met initial guidance, but forward guidance is not raised; management flags specific headwinds (Mexico excise tax, divestitures, weak consumer demand in China/India) and uses cautious language ('prudent', 'realistic'). The score is slightly positive due to the 2026 EPS growth guidance of 7%-8% versus $3 in 2025, which implies acceleration from 4% growth in 2025, but this is partly attributed to a 3-point currency tailwind, so the organic improvement is modest.

summary.revenue: Organic revenue growth of 5% in Q4 2025 and 7% average annual organic revenue growth since 2017. Full-year 2025 organic revenue growth was in line with long-term growth algorithm.
summary.eps: Comparable EPS of $3.00 in 2025, growing 4% despite a 5-point currency headwind and a 2-point increase in the comparable effective tax rate. Q4 2025 comparable EPS of $0.58, up 6% year-over-year.
summary.guidance: 2026 guidance: organic revenue growth of 4%-5%; comparable currency-neutral EPS growth (ex-M&A) of 5%-6%; comparable EPS growth of 7%-8% versus $3.00 in 2025. Free cash flow expected to be about $12.2 billion.
summary.margin: Comparable gross margin and comparable operating margin both increased approximately 50 basis points in Q4 2025, driven by underlying expansion partially offset by currency headwinds. North America achieved 30% operating margin for the first time.
key_risks: New excise tax in Mexico implemented at the start of 2026, expected volume pressure despite mitigation plans.
Consumer demand in major markets like China and India did not recover to pre-pandemic levels.
Revenue and profit declined in Asia Pacific during Q4 due to softer consumer spending, weaker industry performance, and cycling strong prior-year growth.
Divestitures (sale of Coca-Cola Beverages Africa and CHI Nigeria) will be a back-half weighted headwind to net revenue and EPS in 2026.

Currency headwinds: 5-point headwind to EPS in 2025; 2026 guidance includes a 1-point currency tailwind to net revenues and 3-point tailwind to EPS, but this is a reversal of prior headwinds, not a structural improvement.
key_opportunities: Added 12 billion-dollar brands since 2017, totaling 32 billion-dollar brands; 75% are outside sparkling soft drinks.
Value share gains for the nineteenth consecutive quarter in 2025.
North America achieved 30% operating margin for the first time, with volume, revenue, and comparable operating income all increasing.
Innovation pipeline: Sprite Chill, Coca-Cola Holiday Creamy Vanilla, and new billion-dollar brands (innocent, Santa Clara).
2026 tailwinds: 1-point currency tailwind to net revenues, 3-point currency tailwind to EPS; World Cup in Mexico; 100-year anniversary of system in Mexico.

management_tone.label: cautious
management_tone.justification: Management uses language like 'prudent', 'realistic', 'we are just being a little more realistic', and explicitly flags headwinds (Mexico tax, China/India weakness, divestitures) while maintaining confidence in long-term strategy.

Fourth quarter organic revenue grew 5%, unit case growth was 1%, and concentrate sales grew 3 points ahead of unit cases due to shipment timing and one extra day.
We expect organic revenue growth of 4% to 5%, which is in line with our long-term growth algorithm.
